changes: Illustrative geometry without numerical measurements. Shows reference-frame position coordinates or positive rotations for roll, pitch and yaw; not an experimental result. Editable LaTeX source and matching PDF/PNG/SVG retained. Terminology updated to end effector (EE); schematic point labelled EE. Reference axes explicitly labelled Reference base frame, matching the robot-base expression of end-effector pose. Both pose illustrations use the identical parallel-jaw gripper macro from sources/pose_gripper.tikz, placed at the EE frame origin; a schematic symbol, not an exact tool model. Revised shared gripper to a transparent orthographic side profile with horizontal fingers; all fill and perspective faces removed. Orientation axes run from EE through the outline. User refinement: rotate the gripper -90 degrees so both fingers point downward; show a transparent 3D left-side view with depth edges and no filled faces. Use identical shared geometry and scale in both figures. Latest user refinement: opaque solid gripper with shaded faces and a small positive z rotation (+15 degrees for illustration only), retaining downward fingers and identical geometry/scale. Rotation arcs use smooth paths and clear tangent-aligned arrowheads following the positive right-hand rule. Latest refinement: one continuous opaque gripper body with filled depth faces and no internal edge strokes; further positive yaw so its front faces right. The position illustration adds a schematic chain with seven circular joint markers and connecting links from the base origin to the gripper wrist. Joint chain redrawn with five circles and steadily fanning link inclinations (about 74, 68, 54 and 26 degrees above the horizontal, then 20 below), so the chain leaves the origin between the z axis and the position vector, flattens over the top and drops onto the wrist, where the last circle rests tangentially on the gripper. No circle is drawn at the origin, so the base frame stays visible, and no joint overlaps an axis, the position vector or a projection line. Geometry remains schematic, with no numerical measurements.
